claim: Kanidm's README at v1.12.0 lists passkeys (WebAuthn, incl. attested passkeys), an OAuth2/OIDC authentication provider for SSO, OAuth2/OIDC token exchange, Linux/Unix integration with TPM-protected offline authentication, SSH key distribution, RADIUS, a read-only LDAPS gateway, complete CLI tooling, two-node HA by database replication and a self-service web UI, and says it supports 'small home labs, families, small businesses' up to large enterprise

systemd-sysext (v257.13 man page): extensions are searched in /etc/extensions/, /run/extensions/ and /var/lib/extensions/ (plus /.extra/sysext/ in the initrd); any directory found there is treated as a directory-based extension image and any *.raw file as a disk-image extension; /var/lib/extensions/ is the primary install location; the default --image-policy for sysext is root=verity+signed+encrypted+unprotected+absent:usr=verity+signed+encrypted+unprotected+absent (unsigned images accepted); --mutable= controls write routing [man page has no switch that refuses directory extensions]
